claims.claim: Attackers got in through a fake job-interview assignment and a tampered Homebrew installer

claims.fix: Post describes both as stages of a multi-stage campaign (Homebrew in June on Engineer A, fake interview in September on Engineer B, whose machine was the springboard); it does not explicitly name the initial entry point for the 29 Oct attack.

claims.claim: attackers used the token on 29 October to deploy a container and run a malicious script

claims.fix: Detail: done from Engineer C's computer using Engineer A's stolen credentials.

claims.claim: It doesn't name the AI tool or give indicators of compromise
claims.quote: refers only to 'an internal AI tool'; no hashes, IPs, domains or wallet addresses; but lists file paths such as /opt/homebrew/Cellar/pyenv/2.8.0/libexec/pyenv and links a SANS diary; 'Some technical details will remain confidential'
claims.fix: Tool is not named (true). No hashes/domains/wallet addresses, but the post does list file-level paths from the malicious pyenv replacement and links a SANS diary on the tampered Homebrew; say 'no hashes, domains or addresses'.

claims.claim: Stopgap: not stated in the post
